title: Significant modulation of acoustoelectric current associated with charge density wave transitions
authors: Natsumi Nikaido, Takuya Kawada, Koji Fujiwara, Jihoon Park, Nan Jiang, Kouta Kondou, Shintaro Takada, Yasuhiro Niimi
abstract: We studied acoustoelectric (AE) currents in materials that undergo charge density wave (CDW) transitions, induced by a surface acoustic wave (SAW) on a piezoelectric substrate. The polarity and magnitude of the AE current in NbSe$_3$ and 2H-TaSe$_2$ were modulated due to their CDW transitions. We also found that the sign of the AE current depends on the SAW propagation direction with respect to the crystalline axis of the substrate.A phenomenological model assuming strain-modified conductivity can qualitatively account for the significant modulation of the AE current associated with the CDW transition, as well as the SAW propagation orientation dependence. The present results offer a powerful probe for exploring SAW-electron interactions in van der Waals materials, thereby highlighting their potential for advancing the emerging field of straintronics.
summary: This work explores the acoustoelectric effect in materials exhibiting charge density waves (CDWs) using surface acoustic waves (SAWs). The researchers found that the AE current is significantly modulated by CDW transitions and depends on the SAW propagation direction. A strain-modified conductivity model successfully accounts for these complex, anisotropic transport phenomena.
main_problem: The study investigates how charge density wave (CDW) transitions modulate the acoustoelectric (AE) current generated by surface acoustic waves (SAWs) in layered materials.
main_result: The AE current exhibits significant modulation and polarity changes correlated with CDW transitions and the SAW propagation direction, which is explained by a strain-modified conductivity model.
method: The research combines experimental measurements of AE current and resistance using VNA on piezoelectric substrates with the development of a phenomenological model.
model_or_system: The system involves thin films of CDW materials like NbSe3 and 2H-TaSe2 exfoliated onto piezoelectric LiNbO3 substrates. The physics is governed by the coupling between SAW-induced strain/electric fields and the electronic transport properties modulated by CDW formation.
key_observables: AE current polarity and magnitude, dependence on SAW power (P_SAW), and temperature dependence near CDW transition temperatures.
important_parameters: SAW frequency/velocity, SAW power (P_SAW), CDW transition temperatures (e.g., 140 K, 60 K).
main_assumptions: The AE current is modeled as arising from the rectification of the SAW-induced electric field via strain-induced modulation of conductivity.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the SAW device setup, S21 spectra, and plots showing AE current dependence on SAW power and temperature, highlighting modulation near CDW transitions.
paper_structure: The paper structure moves from characterizing the SAW excitation and measuring the AE current to analyzing the modulation effects linked to CDW transitions, culminating in the application of a phenomenological model to explain the observed directional and transition-dependent behavior.
why_interesting: The strong coupling between mechanical strain (from SAWs) and electronic state transitions (CDW) provides a platform for studying non-equilibrium charge transport and strain-mediated quantum phenomena, which is relevant to understanding open quantum systems dynamics.

(e), (f) T dependence of (e) ˜IAE and (f) ρ normalized by the values at T = 190 K for NbSe3 (red), 2H-TaSe2 (blue), Ta (gray and brown) devices.

Figure 2(e) compares the AE current for NbSe3, 2H- TaSe2, and Ta, normalized by their values at 190 K. In contrast to NbSe3 and 2H-TaSe2, the AE current in Ta is nearly independent of T and does not exhibit any polarity reversal regardless of the film size. This observation indi- cates that the characteristic T dependence and polarity change of the AE current are specific to CDW materials. We remark that T dependence of ˜IAE does not match that of ρ as shown in Fig. 2(f).
